summary: Buffalo Bills safety Jordan Poyer describes how he quit drinking in 2020 after years of alcoholism and then sought deeper answers to his anxiety and unhappiness through ayahuasca at a retreat in Costa Rica. The experience left him more grounded, appreciative of his family and less ego-driven, though it did not boost his on-field production as Aaron Rodgers claimed it did for him. Poyer is playing a versatile role for the Bills, plans another retreat in March, and is working on an ayahuasca documentary.
one_line: Bills safety Jordan Poyer credits sobriety and an ayahuasca retreat in Costa Rica with changing his perspective, marriage and approach to football.
key_facts: Jordan Poyer has played six previous seasons for the Buffalo Bills and is a captain for the fourth time; he was a Pro Bowl safety last year and an All-Pro the year before.
Poyer is the only NFL player in the past six seasons with 500+ tackles, 20+ interceptions and 10+ sacks.
Poyer stopped drinking after a tequila shot on March 13, 2020 in the Puerto Vallarta airport bar, and turned down a shot at Josh Norman's home in Washington, D.C. a few months later.
Poyer's drinking alter ego was called 'Deejay Poyo'; he would down a six-pack of IPAs in 20 to 30 minutes and often blacked out.
Poyer married Rachel Bush in 2018; they have a daughter, Aliyah, and Rachel has more than 4 million Instagram followers.
Poyer was a seventh-round pick in the 2013 NFL draft, was cut six games into his rookie season, and has outlasted 191 of the 217 players drafted ahead of him.
After the 2022 season, Poyer attended a retreat at Resonance in Costa Rica with three ayahuasca ceremonies over a week, preceded by a month of restricted diet.
During the first ceremony Poyer says the 'highest version' of himself lectured him, telling him he wasn't appreciating his wife, daughter, family or house.
Poyer weighed 179 pounds before OTAs last April, about 20 pounds below his playing weight, but the weight came back quickly.
Ayahuasca has not improved Poyer's football performance; he is the Bills' second-leading tackler but says he has not made as many big plays as he would like.
Poyer has turned off Instagram DMs, deleted his Twitter/X account, and plays crystal bowls on Fridays with Taylor Rapp and Will Greenberg at Bills headquarters.
Poyer's biological father, Louis Dunbar, has served multiple prison stints; Poyer says ayahuasca helped him let go of resentment toward him.
The Bills have an out in Poyer's contract after this season; he plans to return to Resonance in March and work on an ayahuasca documentary.
